title: perf(canary): automated detection for latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Reduce mean-time-to-detect performance regressions during rollouts by integrating an automated detector into the perf-canary pipeline and adding enforceable rollout guards. This PR adds a statistical detector for latency and throughput regressions, a hysteresis-based rollout guard component, and operational hooks for automatic rollback or traffic throttling. | What this changes: 1) perf/canary/detector: new detector implementing paired-sample and non-parametric tests for latency/throughput with configurable sensitivity and sample windows; 2) perf/canary/guard: rollout guard that computes confidence and applies throttling/rollback policies with hysteresis; 3) CI pipeline: new perf-canary workflow that runs continuous evaluation during canary traffic; 4) docs: operator guide and tuning notes; 5) tests: unit and integration tests with synthetic workload. | Design notes: detector uses bootstrapped confidence intervals and optional baseline-window alignment to tolerate traffic drift; default sensitivity tuned to produce ~1 false positive/week on production traffic based on historical traces. Rollout guard has two thresholds: warning (emit alert and reduce canary qps by 50%) and critical (initiate automatic rollback after grace period). Hysteresis prevents flip-flopping during transient spikes. | Checklist: - [x] Detector implementation + unit tests - [x] Guard implementation + integration tests - [x] CI workflow + test matrix - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Load-tested on perf-canary lab (synthetic tails) | Risk: Automatic rollback enabled behind feature flag per-customer and per-cluster; rollout policy defaults to manual confirmation for first 24h after deploy. Metrics added: canary.latency.delta_p95, canary.throughput.delta_rps, canary.regression.confidence.

review_conversation: Jordan Kim (reviewer): Nice work - high level looks good. A few requests: (1) Can you add a short note on how sample-window alignment handles traffic shift? (2) Tests: add a regression test that simulates a noisy tail to ensure hysteresis avoids flapping.

Aisha Patel (author): Responding - added section in docs about window alignment (docs/perf/canary.md) and added integration test that simulates tail spikes (tests/perf/test_canary_guard_integration.py).
Mateo Ruiz (reviewer): The detector uses bootstrapping - what's the default sample size? Also suggest exposing sensitivity via a cluster-level config so SRE can tune without redeploy.
Aisha Patel (author): Default bootstrap samples set to 1000 (can be tuned). Exposed sensitivity and bootstrap-samples in helm values (infra/helm/canary-values.yaml) and runtime flags.
Priya Desai (approver): Verified test coverage and load test results in perf lab. Approving, please squash-merge after resolving the one CI flake in perf-canary workflow.

release_notes: Adds automated performance-canary detection (latency & throughput) and rollout guards with hysteresis. Feature gated behind canary.auto_detection and can be tuned via helm values. Includes operator guide and runbook.
testing_notes: Load-tested in perf-canary lab with p50/p95/p99 tails including synthetic spike scenarios. Default sensitivity tuned to ~1 false positive/week on historical traffic. Integration tests include a simulated noisy tail to validate hysteresis.
operational_steps: To enable automatic rollback set infra.helm.canaryValues.autoDetection=true and set rolloutPolicy to auto in cluster config. For initial rollouts keep autoRollback=false for 24h. Alerts emitted to #sre-canary and PagerDuty if critical threshold breached.
notes_for_release: Operator-visible metrics: canary.latency.delta_p95, canary.throughput.delta_rps, canary.regression.confidence. Helm chart bump recommended. Feature disabled by default for existing customers.
